01.r: Turns to the point of the letter.
01.n: Gesenius: now, already, citing this verse.

02.r: The king is to be informed.
02.n: A passive participle, 'known'. Gesenius cites this verse for the phrase 'be it known to the king'.

03.r: A wish or polite command: let this be known.
03.n: The brief's lexicon notes this use of the verb 'to be' with the participle of knowing, to let something become known.

04.r: The Persian king to whom the letter is written.

05.r: Introduces what the king should know.

06.r: Sets out the condition the writers warn of.
06.n: Gesenius: behold, surely; whether; if. Here 'if'.

07.r: Jerusalem, which the returned Jews are rebuilding.

09.r: If the city's rebuilding is completed.
09.n: A passive form: 'it will be built'.

10.r: The city walls, the sign of a city able to defend itself.

11.n: Gesenius: to finish, to perfect, and he cites this verse for the passive form.

12.r: The regular payment owed to the Persian king.
12.n: Our register renders this word 'tribute'. BDB: tribute; Gesenius treats it as the same word as another Aramaic word for tribute. The KJV and YLT put the three levies in a different order, calling this one 'toll'.

13.r: A second levy, kept apart from the tribute.
13.n: Our register renders this word 'duty'. Gesenius: a species of tribute, probably imposed on articles consumed, an excise, citing this verse. The KJV calls it 'tribute', JPS 'impost', ASV 'custom'.

14.r: A third levy, charged on travel.
14.n: Gesenius: a way-toll, citing this verse; the brief's lexicon gives its root as the verb 'to walk'. Our register renders it 'road toll', keeping 'toll' for the Greek τέλος in the New Testament. The KJV says 'custom' and the DRC 'yearly revenues'.

16.r: The payments the people will refuse.
16.n: Gesenius: to give, citing this verse; STEPBible tags this occurrence with the sense 'pay'.

17.r: The outcome for the king's income.
17.n: A rare Persian word found only here, and its sense is uncertain. Gesenius: perhaps 'at length, in the end', from a Persian word for end, and he notes the Greek renders it 'and this'. The brief's lexicon gives 'treasury' or 'revenue', which the KJV ('the revenue of the kings') and the BSB follow.

18.r: The Persian kings, the reigning one and those after him.
18.n: Plural and without the article in the Aramaic: 'kings'.

19.n: Gesenius: to damage anyone, citing this verse. The form can be read as 'it will damage' or 'you will damage'; the KJV and JPS take the second, 'thou shalt endamage'.

_extra.19: ἔσονταί (will be): the Greek says 'tributes will not be yours', adding a clause the Aramaic does not have.
_extra.20: σοι (to you): part of the same added clause.

12.n: φόροι, 'tributes': φόρος is the word our register renders 'tribute' in the New Testament. The Greek has nothing for the duty and the road toll.

17.n: καὶ τοῦτο, 'and this': Gesenius notes that the Greek renders the rare word this way.
